description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Côte d'Ivoire Country Programme works to tackle the physical and regulatory trade bottlenecks that constrain one of West Africa's fastest-growing economies, operating since 2024 along the Abidjan–Lagos Corridor, a route marked by over 60 checkpoints that add significant cost and delay to regional trade despite Côte d'Ivoire's active membership of AfCFTA, ECOWAS, and UEMOA. The Programme operates across three interconnected levels: at the regional level, supporting alignment of national trade policy and customs procedures with AfCFTA and ECOWAS frameworks, modernising SPS and standards systems, and advancing interoperable single window and electronic certification infrastructure; at the corridor level, working alongside ECOWAS to translate infrastructure ambitions into investable pipelines and streamlining inspections and inter-agency coordination along the Abidjan–Lagos Corridor through the SWIFT multi-country programme; and at the country level, building the export competitiveness of high-potential sectors (cocoa, cashew nuts, fisheries, and cotton) by upgrading SPS systems, expanding SME access to certification and finance, and supporting Côte d'Ivoire's National Development Plan ambition to shift from raw commodity exports to value-added production, while the Making Trade Work for Women programme targets 80,000 traders, 70% of them women, across six West African countries including Côte d'Ivoire, through financial inclusion, digital market access, and climate resilience support.

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.
